kypExtensions.summary: The staircase grammar of the Kaplan-Meier figure: every curve starts at 1.0 (all enrollees event-free — both printed arms share the opening flat segment); each event time is a vertical step down sized by the printed arithmetic 'Survival probability = 1 – (event probability)'; flats between events mean no events; endpoint dots at the end of follow-up (the printed Z) mean the curve stops without a further drop; and the two-arm reading keeps HEIGHT (survivors so far) and SLOPE (hazard) as separate questions — the higher curve is the better arm, the steeper curve the sicker one.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the definition sentences and the unlabeled figure; the element-by-element grammar, the censoring/end-of-follow-up gloss of the endpoint dots (the print gives no legend for X, Y, Z or the dots), and the height-vs-slope distinction are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea MOVES 1–2 + mechanisms[0] km-curve-grammar + blocks[2] the decoder list + blocks[3] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A annotation rail

kypExtensions.summary: The hazard-ratio direction apparatus: HR as a ratio of the named group's hazard to the comparator's, anchored at the null HR = 1; HR > 1 — the event (eg, death, relapse) occurs more frequently in the treatment/exposure group (the steeper arm — a HARM signal for adverse events); HR < 1 — less frequently (protective effect — the flatter, higher arm, the printed Drug curve's geometry); the harm/help framing for adverse-event outcomes, the named-group-is-the-index rule, and the desirable-event caveat are the KYP wrapper around the three printed bullets.
kypExtensions.rationale: The three bullets are printed; the index-group rule, the harm/benefit gloss, the see-saw organization, and the desirable-event caveat are KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea MOVE 3 + mechanisms[1] hazard-ratio-slopes + blocks[4] the compare block + the registry visual's Zone B trio cards

kypExtensions.summary: The printed bridge sentence developed into the figure-reading rule: HR is derived from the relative slopes (hazards) of the survival curves — judge hazard by STEEPNESS (a steeper curve = higher hazard, faster occurrence of event), never by height; the separation of curves over time reflects the magnitude of HR (curves hugging = HR near 1; curves prying apart = HR far from 1), with the P value for the survival difference from log rank test or Cox regression.
kypExtensions.rationale: The bridge sentence and its two bullets are printed; the slopes-not-heights naming, the hug/pry geometry reading, and the log-rank-vs-Cox division of labor (curves compared whole vs hazards fitted) are KYP's development.
kypExtensions.location: core.why + core.keyIdea MOVES 3–4 + blocks[3] MOVE 5 + the registry visual's Zone C slope/separation panels

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the two printed blocks — 4 patterns (the figure-reading stem, the HR-interpretation stem, the test-selection stem, the slope-identification stem), 4 traps (height vs slope; HR vs RR; HR > 1 vs < 1 direction with the named index group; survival vs event probability via the printed complement), 3 pivots (HR < 1 = protective not 'less effective'; unequal follow-up/censoring routes to KM; the survival-difference test family), and 8 recall cards covering both blocks plus the figure.
